pathways.label: Conviction or diversion expungement under K.S.A. 21-6614
pathways.summary: The petition identifies whether relief is requested for a conviction or diversion and includes arrest, charge, court, disposition, and final-discharge facts. The form provides offense-dependent one-, three-, five-, or ten-year periods after diversion completion, sentence satisfaction, or discharge from supervision. The person must not have been convicted of a felony in the prior two years and no felony proceeding may be pending or being instituted. The offense cannot be one of the…
ruleClauses: The petition identifies whether relief is requested for a conviction or diversion and includes arrest, charge, court, disposition, and final-discharge facts.
The form provides offense-dependent one-, three-, five-, or ten-year periods after diversion completion, sentence satisfaction, or discharge from supervision.
The person must not have been convicted of a felony in the prior two years and no felony proceeding may be pending or being instituted.
The offense cannot be one of the no-expungement offenses listed in K.S.A. 21-6614(e).
A person required to register as a sex or violent offender cannot receive expungement while registration is required.
The petition is filed in the county of arrest, followed by notice, a hearing, and proposed grant/denial orders.
waitingRules: The form provides offense-dependent one-, three-, five-, or ten-year periods after diversion completion, sentence satisfaction, or discharge from supervision.
The person must not have been convicted of a felony in the prior two years and no felony proceeding may be pending or being instituted.
exclusionRules: The offense cannot be one of the no-expungement offenses listed in K.S.A. 21-6614(e).
A person required to register as a sex or violent offender cannot receive expungement while registration is required.

No felony proceeding may be pending or being instituted. The backend must confirm the offense is otherwise eligible before offering the petition packet.
ruleClauses: The form provides a route for a person who successfully completed a specialty court program when the conviction would ordinarily be eligible after three years.

waitingRules: available immediately upon successful completion of the qualifying specialty-court program; no additional elapsed period applies

pathways.label: Municipal conviction or diversion expungement
pathways.summary: Municipal conviction or diversion expungement under Kan. Stat. Ann. § 12-4516. three or more years have elapsed since the petitioner satisfied the sentence imposed or was discharged from probation, parole or a suspended sentence, K.S.A. 12-4516(a)(1), or since the terms of the diversion agreement were fulfilled, K.S.A. 12-4516(a)(2); five years apply to the ordinance violations listed in K.S.A. 12-4516(d) and to a first violation equivalent to K.S.A. 8-1567 under K.S.A. 12-4516(e)(1), ten years apply to a second or subsequent such violation under K.S.A. 12-4516(e)(2), one year applies under K.S.A. 12-4516(c) to a prostitution-equivalent ordinance violation where coercion caused by the act of another is proven, and no elapsed period applies under K.S.A. 12-4516(b) to an ordinance violation prohibited by K.S.A. 12-16,134(a) or (b) and adopted before July 1, 2014.
ruleClauses: three or more years have elapsed since the petitioner satisfied the sentence imposed or was discharged from probation, parole or a suspended sentence, K.S.A. 12-4516(a)(1), or since the terms of the diversion agreement were fulfilled, K.S.A. 12-4516(a)(2); five years apply to the ordinance violations listed in K.S.A. 12-4516(d) and to a first violation equivalent to K.S.A. 8-1567 under K.S.A. 12-4516(e)(1), ten years apply to a second or subsequent such violation under K.S.A. 12-4516(e)(2), one year applies under K.S.A. 12-4516(c) to a prostitution-equivalent ordinance violation where coercion caused by the act of another is proven, and no elapsed period applies under K.S.A. 12-4516(b) to an ordinance violation prohibited by K.S.A. 12-16,134(a) or (b) and adopted before July 1, 2014
waitingRules: three or more years have elapsed since the petitioner satisfied the sentence imposed or was discharged from probation, parole or a suspended sentence, K.S.A. 12-4516(a)(1), or since the terms of the diversion agreement were fulfilled, K.S.A. 12-4516(a)(2); five years apply to the ordinance violations listed in K.S.A. 12-4516(d) and to a first violation equivalent to K.S.A. 8-1567 under K.S.A. 12-4516(e)(1), ten years apply to a second or subsequent such violation under K.S.A. 12-4516(e)(2), one year applies under K.S.A. 12-4516(c) to a prostitution-equivalent ordinance violation where coercion caused by the act of another is proven, and no elapsed period applies under K.S.A. 12-4516(b) to an ordinance violation prohibited by K.S.A. 12-16,134(a) or (b) and adopted before July 1, 2014
This rule governs filings on or after 2015-07-01.
exclusionRules: A conviction or diversion for a city ordinance violation that would also constitute a violation of K.S.A. 8-2,144, commercial driving under the influence, K.S.A. 12-4516(f).
A district court conviction or diversion, which runs under K.S.A. 21-6614.
An arrest with no municipal conviction and no municipal diversion, which runs under K.S.A. 12-4516a.
A petitioner convicted of a felony within the past two years, or against whom such a proceeding is pending or being instituted, K.S.A. 12-4516(h)(1).

timing.anchorText: three or more years have elapsed since the petitioner satisfied the sentence imposed or was discharged from probation, parole or a suspended sentence, K.S.A. 12-4516(a)(1), or since the terms of the diversion agreement were fulfilled, K.S.A. 12-4516(a)(2); five years apply to the ordinance violations listed in K.S.A. 12-4516(d) and to a first violation equivalent to K.S.A. 8-1567 under K.S.A. 12-4516(e)(1), ten years apply to a second or subsequent such violation under K.S.A. 12-4516(e)(2), one year applies under K.S.A. 12-4516(c) to a prostitution-equivalent ordinance violation where coercion caused by the act of another is proven, and no elapsed period applies under K.S.A. 12-4516(b) to an ordinance violation prohibited by K.S.A. 12-16,134(a) or (b) and adopted before July 1, 2014

requiredFacts: The defendant's full name, and the full name used at the time of arrest, conviction or diversion if different?
Sex, race and date of birth?
The crime for which the defendant was arrested, convicted or diverted?
The date of the arrest, conviction or diversion?
The identity of the convicting court, the arresting law enforcement agency or the diverting authority?
Was this a conviction of a city ordinance violation, or a fulfilled diversion agreement based on one?
Would the ordinance violation also have constituted an offence listed in K.S.A. 12-4516(c), (d) or (e)?
The date the sentence was satisfied, the date of discharge from probation, parole or a suspended sentence, or the date the diversion terms were fulfilled?
Has the petitioner been convicted of a felony in the past two years, or is any such proceeding pending or being instituted?
Does the convicting municipal court publish its own expungement instrument, or govern expungement by charter ordinance?
exclusions: A conviction or diversion for a city ordinance violation that would also constitute a violation of K.S.A. 8-2,144, commercial driving under the influence, K.S.A. 12-4516(f).
A district court conviction or diversion, which runs under K.S.A. 21-6614.
An arrest with no municipal conviction and no municipal diversion, which runs under K.S.A. 12-4516a.
A petitioner convicted of a felony within the past two years, or against whom such a proceeding is pending or being instituted, K.S.A. 12-4516(h)(1).

legalAuthority.notes: Municipal court only. K.S.A. 21-6614 reaches a municipal case only where it was appealed to the district court; 12-4516 exists for the rest, so this route must never be served by, or map onto, any district-court 21-6614 pathway. Conviction and diversion are branches inside one mechanism, not two mechanisms: the statute gives one destination, one petition structure with six prescribed contents, one notice rule and one set of three findings.

pathways.label: Municipal arrest record expungement
pathways.summary: Municipal arrest record expungement under Kan. Stat. Ann. § 12-4516a. available on any one of the five grounds stated in K.S.A. 12-4516a(c) — arrest by mistaken identity, no probable cause found by a court, a finding of not guilty, dismissal of the charges or no charges filed and none likely to be filed, an arrest on an ordinance prohibited by K.S.A. 12-16,134, or that expungement is in the best interests of justice — and K.S.A. 12-4516a states no elapsed waiting period of any kind.
ruleClauses: available on any one of the five grounds stated in K.S.A. 12-4516a(c) — arrest by mistaken identity, no probable cause found by a court, a finding of not guilty, dismissal of the charges or no charges filed and none likely to be filed, an arrest on an ordinance prohibited by K.S.A. 12-16,134, or that expungement is in the best interests of justice — and K.S.A. 12-4516a states no elapsed waiting period of any kind
waitingRules: available on any one of the five grounds stated in K.S.A. 12-4516a(c) — arrest by mistaken identity, no probable cause found by a court, a finding of not guilty, dismissal of the charges or no charges filed and none likely to be filed, an arrest on an ordinance prohibited by K.S.A. 12-16,134, or that expungement is in the best interests of justice — and K.S.A. 12-4516a states no elapsed waiting period of any kind
This rule governs filings on or after 2015-07-01.
exclusionRules: A municipal conviction or a fulfilled municipal diversion, which runs under K.S.A. 12-4516.
An arrest on a state law violation, which runs under K.S.A. 22-2410 in the district court.

timing.anchorText: available on any one of the five grounds stated in K.S.A. 12-4516a(c) — arrest by mistaken identity, no probable cause found by a court, a finding of not guilty, dismissal of the charges or no charges filed and none likely to be filed, an arrest on an ordinance prohibited by K.S.A. 12-16,134, or that expungement is in the best interests of justice — and K.S.A. 12-4516a states no elapsed waiting period of any kind

requiredFacts: The petitioner's full name, and the full name used at the time of arrest if different?
Sex, race and date of birth?
The crime for which the petitioner was arrested?
The date of the arrest?
The identity of the arresting law enforcement agency?
Which of the statutory grounds under K.S.A. 12-4516a(c) is relied on?
Was the arrest made on a city ordinance charge rather than a state law violation?
Was the petitioner arrested as a result of being a victim of identity theft under K.S.A. 21-6107 or former K.S.A. 21-4018?
Does the municipal court where the ordinance charge was brought publish its own expungement instrument?
exclusions: A municipal conviction or a fulfilled municipal diversion, which runs under K.S.A. 12-4516.
An arrest on a state law violation, which runs under K.S.A. 22-2410 in the district court.

sourceSections.title: Sign the Petition for Expungement of Conviction or Diversion. Your signature is your
sourceSections.text:
affirmation that all of the information in the petition is accurate to the best of your
knowledge.

4. File the original petition and required number of copies with the Clerk of the Court in the
county in which you were arrested and pay the required docket fee. (You will need to check
with the Clerk to find out how many copies are required.)

sourceSections.title: If you do not know the case number of the matter for which you are seeking expungement, you
sourceSections.text:
may obtain the case number from the Clerk of the Court when you file.

6. Contact the Clerk of the Court or the Administrative Assistant of the judge to which the case
has been assigned, and ask for a date and time for a hearing before the court. Ask for the
division or room number of the hearing as well.

7. Complete the Notice of Hearing and make 2 additional copies. File the original notice and
copies with the Clerk of the Court who will send a copy to the office of the attorney who
prosecuted your case and the arresting law enforcement agency.

* Based on State v. Anderson, 12 Kan. App. 2d 342, 744 P.2d 143 (1987), the law in effect at the time of the offense
applies with regard to eligibility for expungement unless the current law is more beneficial to the defendant. The
current statute, K.S.A. 21-6614(d)(2), says a second or subsequent DUI conviction under K.S.A. 8-1567 cannot be
expunged until 10 or more years have elapsed, but from July 1, 2014, to June 30, 2015, the statute allowed any DUI
conviction or diversion to be expunged after 7 years. L. 2014 Ch. 102, § 6, effective July 1, 2014; L. 2015 Ch. 71, §
4, effective July 1, 2015. For a first DUI conviction or diversion, the current law, allowing expungement after 5 years,
applies because it is more beneficial to a defendant than the 7 years required from July 1, 2014, to June 30, 2015. For
a second or subsequent DUI conviction, the current statute, K.S.A. 21-6614(d)(2), does not allow expungement until
10 or more years have elapsed. Therefore, for second or subsequent DUIs that were committed on July 1, 2014,
through June 30, 2015, the statute in effect at the time of the crime that allowed expungement after 7 years applies
because it is more beneficial to the defendant.
+
Completion of a Specialty Court Program
A person who has completed the requirements of a specialty court program may petition for immediate expungement
of any offense which is otherwise eligible for expungement after 3 years. This early expungement opportunity does
not apply to offenses for which expungement is not available or to offenses which require a 1, 5, 7 or 10-year waiting
period.

Rev. KSJC 08/2022 6
